Move numbers in this file are 0-based, as in the reviews.
ENGINE VARIABLES used in conditions: 3 VAR_HAVE_MSG (0 = no line; 0xFF while a line prints, wait() parts included; 1 while its last part times out: engines/scumm/actor.cpp:3530, engines/scumm/string.cpp:1227, engines/scumm/scumm.cpp:3382), 5 VAR_OVERRIDE, 25 VAR_TALK_ACTOR (the actor whose line is up; 1 = Guybrush), 32 VAR_VERB_SCRIPT, 52 VAR_CURSORSTATE, 53 VAR_USERPUT (engines/scumm/vars.cpp:38-94; 52/53 mirror _cursor.state/_userPut, script_v5.cpp:934-936), 103/104 (the last sentence's first and second object, written only by global/script-002.txt [0030]-[0035] when global 2 takes a sentence), and 352, the scripts' own cutscene depth: global/script-018.txt [0000] Var[352] += 1 at every cutscene(), global/script-019.txt [0000] Var[352] -= 1 at every endCutscene, no other writer in data/scripts-dos-cd (S4 uses it the same way). Cutscene start/end scripts are 18/19 (global/script-001.txt [0592]-[0597]); '.' is VAR_TALKSTOP_KEY 46 ([0817]); Esc is VAR_CUTSCENEEXIT_KEY 27 ([0092]).
ENGINE CONFIG (required): skip_text = False and skip_cutscenes = False. src/speedrun/engine.py:108-109 turns both on by default and passes them once, at engine start, as SPEEDRUN_SKIP_TEXT and SPEEDRUN_SKIP_CUTSCENES (:255-258). The bridge then presses Esc on every frame a live override exists while _userPut <= 0 and '.' on every line (patches/0001-scumm-add-speedrun-bridge.patch: maybeInjectSkip() runs every frame, cutsceneSkipEffective(), textSkipEffective()); the control-socket executor has no per-move no_skip (stepForbidsCutsceneSkip() reads only the C4 plan). With them on, the store reading (move 92: its cutscene([2]) takes userput 1 -> 0 through global/script-018.txt [0007], override at room-059-stans/obj-0732-magnetic-compass.txt [0026]) is Esc'd on its first frame, before local 214 can run inside it, so no slide forms; every stall reading is aborted at once; and the lines that keep global 70 waiting are '.'-skipped, which shortens the carry. Moves 0-89 work in either mode (their key moves then find nothing left to press); from move 90 (store entry) to the end the skips must be off. With today's bridge that means the whole engine run (open_questions: S1, S2 and S4 assume the auto-skips). Every '.' and Esc of S3 is an explicit move.
KEY RULES (play() in src/speedrun/executor.py presses a key once, on the frame after `after` holds; these moves need the repeat behaviour below, see open_questions). K-ESC (key 'esc'): from the first frame after `after` holds, press Esc on each frame on which it takes effect, i.e. a live, non-stale override exists at the current cutscene level (abortCutscene acts only when cutScenePtr[level] != 0, engines/scumm/script.cpp:1689-1707; the bridge's override tracker, cutsceneSkipEffective() without its _userPut test, computes exactly this), until the override pointer it pressed on is gone (the tracker no longer reports that level/pointer, or the cutscene level dropped); if the same pointer is still live on the next frame, press again. VAR_OVERRIDE (var 5) is no use as the test: abortCutscene sets it to 1, but the resumed script's endOverride or endCutscene clears it in the same slice. Then, unless the move says 'no '.' part', press '.' on each frame on which a line is showing and would not end this frame (var 3 != 0 and _talkDelay > delta: textSkipEffective()) until `until` holds. K-DOT (key '.'): only the '.' part of K-ESC; a move that names talkers presses only on frames where var 25 is one of them. K-CHOOSE (choose): press the line's digit key (menu verbs 120-128 get keys from 49 = '1' up, global/script-032.txt [0005]) on the first frame the menu takes it (var 194 == 0 after the menu build, _userPut > 0). Global 14 then echoes the line as Guybrush (printEgo, WaitForMessage, two breakHere: global/script-014.txt [00F2]-[0101]) before it sets Var[194] ([0105]), because every menu option sets its Bit[384+k] and so Bit[118] = 0 ([002C]-[0033]); press '.' on that echo, only on frames where var 3 != 0 and var 25 == 1, until `until` holds. Without it every choice waits a full line (60 jiffies, 12 frames at talkspeed 255).
SLIDE GATE (kind = glitch): the executor's click gate (wait_gate() and the choose branch, both _run(control=True)) waits for the bridge's clickGateOpen(), which needs cutSceneStackPointer == 0. From move 97 to the exit global 70's cutscene stays open (var 352 >= 1), so those clicks and choices would never be issued. The engine accepts input whenever _userPut > 0 (engines/scumm/verbs.cpp:590, no cutscene test), which is what the slide provides. Every kind-glitch move from move 98 on is issued on the first frame its `after` holds (each includes var 53 == 1 and, for clicks, var 352 == 1 so that no other cutscene is open), with room != 0 and the target visible (the inventory slot; a room object on screen with the hover script running; for a menu, var 194 == 0), whatever cs is. Room objects can be targeted only while the hover script global 23 runs unfrozen: the map look (move 98) restarts it, and every later cutscene freezes and unfreezes it symmetrically.
CARRY (moves 97-116): global 70 must still be inside its first cutscene (global/script-070.txt [0066]-[0211]) when room-083-cu-dock/local-200.txt [0C6E] hard-sets userput; exit.flags var 352 == 2 checks it. Optional stall blocks J (moves 100-102), H (104-106) and L (108-110) freeze global 70 during the three long walks; the search picks which to keep. Never press '.' on a line of global 70 in this window (Otis's lines in the jail and in room 83 after [05F2]).
TALKSPEED (cross-segment constraint): the project pins talkspeed 255 (docs/comparison.md, VAR_CHARINC = 0; S1 notes ask to pick it once for the run). At 255 every text part lasts 60 jiffies = 12 frames at delta 5 (engines/scumm/string.cpp:1142, :1312), so the store reading is about 24 frames and the compass click has a narrow window (see the ITEM SLIDE move). Slower text widens that window and lengthens each stall reading, and costs nothing on lines skipped with '.'; if the run keeps 255, the window and the carry budget must be re-measured at 255. Walk legs marked SHMOOVE in their notes are candidates for the per-frame re-click micro-search (docs/research/anypercent-engine-mechanics.md section 2.5). RENUMBERED: stall blocks H2 (moves 107-109) and L2 (114-116) were added after the engine runs; moves from the old 107 on moved by 3, from the old 111 on by 6.
